summary.headline: Raymond Q2 FY27 total income rose 21% YoY to INR683 crores with EBITDA margin of 15.1%; aerospace revenue up 72% to INR139 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income for Q2 FY27 was INR683 crores (up 21% YoY) with EBITDA of INR103 crores at a 15.1% margin; H1 total income was INR1,311 crores (up 17%) with EBITDA of INR203 crores (15.5%). Aerospace (JK Maini Global Aerospace) led growth, with revenue up 72% YoY to INR139 crores at 21% EBITDA margin. Precision technology and auto components grew 15% YoY to INR471 crores at 13% margin, and the company operationalised its automotive aftermarket business in August. Management said Q2 costs (raw materials, tooling, freight) remained elevated, with raw materials largely passed through to customers under contracts. Management committed to mid-20s aerospace growth going forward rather than 40%.

segments.name: Aerospace (JK Maini Global Aerospace Ltd)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR139 crores (+72% YoY), EBITDA INR29 crores at 21% margin; H1 revenue INR262 crores (+56%) at 21.1% margin. Growth driven by commercial ramp-up of newly commissioned capacity.

segments.name: Precision Technology & Auto Components (JK Maini Precision Technology Ltd)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR471 crores (+15% YoY), EBITDA INR61 crores at 13% margin. H1 revenue INR915 crores (+13%), EBITDA INR122 crores (+24%), margin 13.4%. Company describes the business as net debt-free.

segments.name: Automotive aftermarket (new, within B2C)
segments.commentary: Operationalised in Q2 FY27 (entered market in August) with about 800 part numbers; no revenue or margin numbers disclosed, management said it is growing off a smaller base.

guidance_outlook: Aerospace growth commitment moderated to mid-20s percent going forward; management explicitly declined to commit to 40%.
Current Bangalore aerospace facility capacity expected to reach INR700-750 crores revenue (up from earlier INR600-650 crore indication) before Andhra Pradesh greenfield comes online.
Andhra Pradesh greenfield facility targeted to produce output in Q3 FY28 (December 2027); brownfield facility to start production in the current year.
Tools and hardware (T&H) business expected to grow at double-digit average, with about 50% of planned new products launched in the last 3 months.
Nozzle guide vane capacity doubling from 8,000 to 16,000 units per year; machines installed, about 45 days to run before ramp-up, revenue expected to reflect from the following quarter.
Greenfield Andhra total commitment INR1,000 crores across aero and auto over 5 years; about INR400 crores expected to be spent by the time the factory starts.
capex_capacity: Andhra Pradesh greenfield (aero and auto mega factory) on track for output in Q3 FY28 (December 2027); about INR400 crores expected spent by start-up within total INR1,000 crores over 5 years.

Brownfield facility in Andhra Pradesh set up as interim capacity augmentation, 2-3 km from the greenfield site; starts automotive production this year and doubles as a training ground for aero and precision technology.
Bangalore aerospace facility: machines, space, layout changes, mezzanine floors and cycle-time reductions adding capacity to INR700-750 crores revenue potential.
Nozzle guide vane capacity doubling from 8,000 to 16,000 units/year; machines arrived.

Approval timelines: aerospace customer approval 3-6 months; automotive 3 to 8-9 months depending on validation. Parts already made will be transferred to Andhra to speed plant approval; company is engaging 5-6 customers about a year in advance.
Machines are brought in modularly a couple of months before dispatch; management says no large breakeven threshold is needed.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand supported by pre-festive channel restocking in passenger vehicles and premium 2-wheelers; exports shifting from post-destocking replenishment to multi-year production schedules.
Global Tier 1 OEMs derisking supply chains; management cites strong inquiries and order wins for complex precision machine parts and drivetrain subassemblies.
Aerospace: Tier 1 integrators moved from buffer inventory to just-in-time dispatches; shipset value per aircraft rising as customers give larger integrated subassemblies.
Raw materials are passed through to customers under contracts with a lag; freight and tooling cost recovery is negotiated case by case, and management expects some price increases going forward.
Management said order book is incrementally higher than before but did not quantify it; it cited OEM backlogs exceeding 12 years and long-life platform contracts.
Aerospace market share: about 35% in some parts and 65% in others on LEAP; 65%-share parts are about 45% of LEAP content.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised maximum aerospace revenue potential at the Bangalore facility, and what is the brownfield Andhra capacity worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Potential raised to about INR700 crores, with a stretch target of INR750 crores, versus the earlier INR600-650 crores indication. The brownfield Andhra unit is mainly automotive and training; aerospace stays in Bangalore until the greenfield is approved.

qa_highlights.question: Will aerospace growth be sustained at 40%+ into FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to mid-20s growth, not 40%, and said the current Bangalore capacity would still not be fully used by the end of FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the automotive aftermarket business in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No numbers given; about 800 part numbers launched in August, with aftermarket expected to carry better margins than OE in many cases. Update promised next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can raw material and freight cost increases be passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw materials are fully passed through with a lag. Freight is negotiated in some contracts; tooling cost recovery is being negotiated. Operating leverage offset part of the cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the greenfield Andhra investment to date and capital allocation of the warrant proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores to be spent by factory start in December 2027, within a INR1,000 crore total commitment over 5 years. Warrant proceeds are a war chest for inorganic growth held at the holdco; debt sits in operating companies.

qa_highlights.question: Is the greenfield commissioning deferred?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it was always targeted for Q3 of FY28 (December 2027); the earlier reference was a financial-versus-calendar year confusion.

risks_watch: Aerospace margin dilution from R&D write-offs (about 4% of revenue) as new parts are developed daily; Q2 aerospace margin 21% versus higher Q4 seasonality.
Andhra greenfield execution: customer approvals (3-6 months aero, 3-9 months auto) and ramp-up timing; start targeted December 2027.
Input and freight cost inflation and global shipping disruption requiring safety stock, which pressures working capital.
Aerospace reliance on a few OEM/engine programs (LEAP) and on Indian suppliers qualifying for Inconel/titanium raw materials (2-3 year process).
Aftermarket and new adjacencies (medical, gas turbine, defense) are early-stage and unquantified; management said plans would come in about 6 months.
Inorganic acquisition still pending with no timeline; warrant proceeds are earmarked for it.
summary.management_tone: Confident on aerospace demand and capacity, but deliberately cautious on numbers: management declined to quantify order book, aftermarket revenue, and aerostructure margins, and moderated growth guidance to mid-20s. Answers on segment splits and naming were sometimes evasive or repeated the same points.
key_quotes: So, our ultimate goal would be to try and get it to INR750 crores, but yes, we would probably end up somewhere between INR700 crores and INR750 crores.
But my commitment to the market will be in the high mid -20s. We're not going to commit to you that we'll do 40%.
We've not deferred anything by 1 quarter. We were always going to do it in the third quarter of FY28. So, nothing is postponed.
